articles.headline: Klay Thompson blows out shoe as Heat take on Thunder
articles.description: Klay Thompson blew out part of a shoe while defending a fast break in the Heat's game against the Thunder on Sunday night.
articles.headlineJa: クレイ・トンプソン、ヒート対サンダー戦でシューズが破損
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜夜に行われたヒート対サンダーの試合中、クレイ・トンプソンがファストブレイクの守備中にシューズの一部を破損させた。
articles.body:
MIAMI -- Klay Thompson blew out part of a shoe while defending a fast break in the Miami Heat's game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday night.

Thompson was defending a drive by Thunder guard Ajay Mitchell when it appeared a part of his shoe -- possibly an insert -- somehow detached itself with about 5 minutes left in the opening quarter. Mitchell scored, and play was stopped moments later when referees noticed that part of the shoe was around midcourt.

Miami called timeout, and Thompson was lacing up his right shoe on the bench moments later.

Thompson returned to the game midway through the second quarter. He is fourth on the NBA's all-time 3-pointers made list, on pace to catch former Heat guard Ray Allen for the No. 3 spot by the end of November.

articles.headline: Giants intercept Trevor Lawrence twice as they hold on to beat the Jaguars 23-18
articles.description: — J.J. McCarthy threw a touchdown pass to Malik Nabers, Abdul Carter and the defense flustered Trevor Lawrence throughout and the New York Giants held on to defeat the Jacksonville Jaguars 23-18 on Sunday, bouncing back from a bad loss and ending the...
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツ、トレバー・ローレンスから2つのインターセプトを奪い、ジャガーズに23-18で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: J.J.マッカーシーがマリク・ネイバースにタッチダウンパスを決め、アブダル・カーターら守備陣が終始トレバー・ローレンスを翻弄。ニューヨーク・ジャイアンツは日曜、ジャクソンビル・ジャガーズに23-18で競り勝ち、前回の痛い敗戦から立ち直った。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- — J.J. McCarthy threw a touchdown pass to Malik Nabers, Abdul Carter and the defense flustered Trevor Lawrence throughout and the New York Giants held on to defeat the Jacksonville Jaguars 23-18 on Sunday, bouncing back from a bad loss and ending the AFC South leaders' winning streak at three games.


              McCarthy made some important throws to balance out some inaccuracy and was a difference-maker with his legs. He scrambled for 33 yards and was 18 of 38 passing for 173 yards.


              Jameis Winston scored on a quarterback sneak, Dominic Zvada connected on 53- and 54-yard field goals and the Giants (6-3-1) survived Cam Skattebo fumbling for the fifth time this season. The offense that sputtered after going up by 14 points early in the fourth quarter got the job done late to seal the victory.


              Carter had two sacks to double his season total and end a four-game drought without one. His breakout performance came after pledging earlier in the week to show critics what he could do.


              New York did that as a team, 10 days after blowing a late lead against Washington that threatened to damage its chances of winning the NFC East. Beating Jacksonville allowed coach John Harbaugh's team to maintain the same lead atop the division hours after Dallas crushed Tennessee 50-31.


              The Jaguars (7-3) lost for the first time in more than a month, with Lawrence throwing two interceptions and generally looking discombobulated. He was incomplete on a fourth-and-1 pass in the red zone and finished 25 of 47 for 301 yards.


              A lack of a consistent running game did not help Lawrence and the offense, which was without starting center Robert Hainsey, out because of a strained left knee and went 5 of 15 on third down. Jacksonville committed 13 penalties for 107 yards, continuing a troubling trend of undisciplined play.


              Coach Liam Coen challenged a crucial incomplete pass call on what he thought was a TD catch by Parker Washington in the back of the end zone early in the fourth quarter, and officials stuck with the initial ruling after video review.


              Injuries
              Jaguars: Cornerback Jarrian Jones left in the first quarter with a chest injury. ... Left tackle Walker Little left with a knee injury, leading to Wyatt Milum entering. Little was already playing in place of Anton Harrison, who's out for the season. ... Running back Bhayshul Tuten limped off late.


              Giants: Cornerback Greg Newsome injured an ankle on the first defensive series and did not return. ... Linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux got medical attention and departed briefly but returned. 


              Up next
              Jaguars: Host the Tennessee Titans next Sunday.


              Giants: Visit the Indianapolis Colts next Sunday.


              ------

articles.headline: Chargers' Justin Herbert lands in concussion protocol
articles.description: Quarterback Justin Herbert is in the concussion protocol, the Chargers said after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets in Inglewood, California.
articles.headlineJa: チャージャーズのジャスティン・ハーバート、脳震盪プロトコル入り
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日にカリフォルニア州イングルウッドで行われたジェッツ戦で24-27で敗れた後、チャージャーズはクォーターバックのジャスティン・ハーバートが脳震盪プロトコルに入ったことを発表した。
articles.body:
Quarterback Justin Herbert is in the concussion protocol, the Chargers said after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets in Inglewood, California.

Herbert didn't speak to the media after the game, and coach Jim Harbaugh didn't mention the QB's status when he spoke to the media. 

It wasn't immediately clear when Herbert may have been hurt. He had a rushing touchdown in which he somersaulted into the end zone to cut Los Angeles' deficit to 17-10 at the end of the first half.

But he played the entire game, hitting Ladd McConkey with a 6-yard touchdown pass -- their second connection of the game -- on what turned out to be the Chargers' final offensive possession.

Herbert completed 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards with the two TDs to McConkey, but he also got sacked six times in the loss, which dropped Los Angeles to 1-9.

DJ Uiagalelei is next on the depth chart at QB for the Chargers. Trey Lance remain on injured reserve with a groin injury.

The Chargers host the New England Patriots next Sunday.

articles.headline: NFL Week 11 arrivals: George Kittle rocks luchador mask ahead of SNF in Mexico
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第11週の到着シーン：ジョージ・キトル、メキシコでのSNFを前にルチャドールマスクを着用
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスター選手たちは、試合当日のスタジアム到着シーンを毎週のファッションショーに変え続けている。
articles.body:
The forecast affects the game plan for how NFL players put together their Week 11 looks.

And Sunday's arrivals will call for a little more wardrobe strategy.

With morning temperatures near freezing expected in Denver before an afternoon climb into the 40s, players arriving for the Raiders-Broncos game have an opening for coats and chunky knits. Showers in Chicago could make weatherproof outerwear a smart finishing touch, while temperatures approaching 70 in Southern California give the New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers room to keep things lighter.

On the East Coast, Sunday's forecast leaves room for fall outfits without going full winter. Morning temperatures in the 50s in Buffalo should give Miami Dolphins and Buffalo Bills players an opening for sweaters and light jackets, while Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Giants arrivals in East Rutherford, New Jersey, call for similar layers under cloudy skies, with rain possible later in the day.

From practical layers to outfits built for the spotlight, here are the standout arrivals from Week 11.

Sunday's best

Playing in Mexico City on "Sunday Night Football," players from the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings arrived in looks fit for the location. 49ers tight end George Kittle rocked a mask and shirt that paid homage to luchador Penta, while Fred Warner had a Mexico national team kit on. Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. kept his sombrero trend alive in a full mariachi look.

Denver Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton paid homage to former Broncos linebacker Tom Jackson by wearing Jackson's jersey before facing the Las Vegas Raiders. Jackson, a fixture at ESPN as a Hall of Fame broadcaster, died on Friday. He was 75.

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb hit the blue carpet in a plush charcoal jacket, wide-leg plaid trousers and chunky black boots. A scarf tied to his burgundy leather bag added a pop of color to the pregame look.

Bryce Young goes with a modernized throwback flavor to the late 1990s and early 2000s aesthetic. Think Allen Iverson redefining NBA wardrobe attire with the baggy Reebok track pants and hats with titled swag. The modern unique addition here is the pants appear satin-like look that almost looks like Liquid Metal.

Young doesn't make many statements with his words, but he does it with his actions. And this fit feels like he's tapping back into California childhood energy he grew up on. The LA hat slightly titled to the side shows that element too. It translated to his play as the Panthers put up 30-plus points on Baltimore Ravens.

 -- Cameron Wolfe

Thursday night fashion

Texture did the talking in C.J. Stroud's arrival. The Texans quarterback sported a gray knit polo paired with relaxed light-wash jeans, while a black woven bag, brown shoes and a blue-faced watch added the finishing touches.

articles.headline: Jonah Coleman powers Broncos past Raiders 38-24 as Denver honors the late Tom Jackson
articles.description: — Rookie Jonah Coleman ran for a season-best 111 yards and three touchdowns and the Denver Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 on a solemn Sunday in the Mile High City as they honored “Orange Crush” and ESPN great
articles.headlineJa: ジョナ・コールマンがブロンコスを牽引しレイダースに38-24で勝利、デンバーは故トム・ジャクソンを追悼
articles.descriptionJa: ルーキーのジョナ・コールマンがシーズン最高の111ヤード獲得と3つのタッチダウンを記録。デンバー・ブロンコスは、マイルハイシティで「オレンジ・クラッシュ」でありESPNの偉大な人物であった故人を追悼する厳かな日曜を迎え、ラスベガス・レイダースに38-24で勝利した。
articles.body:
DENVER -- — Rookie Jonah Coleman ran for a season-best 111 yards and three touchdowns and the Denver Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 on a solemn Sunday in the Mile High City as they honored “Orange Crush” and ESPN great Tom Jackson following his death at age 75.


              Jackson's death was announced by longtime on-air partner Chris Berman just as some of the Broncos' early risers were starting to arrive at Empower Field for top overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza's first career road start.


              For the coin flip, Broncos great Champ Bailey wore a No. 57 Jackson jersey following a moment of silence and a video tribute to the fiery cornerstone of the defense that led Denver to its first Super Bowl appearance in 1977.


              Ja'Quan McMillian sealed the victory with a 35-yard, one-handed pick-6 with 1:52 remaining and the Broncos (8-2) clinging to a seven-point lead.


              Coleman scored on runs of 1, 4 and 7 yards, the latter two after the Raiders (4-7) had erased a 17-0 deficit.


              The Broncos kept pace with Kansas City atop the AFC West by winning their sixth consecutive game since coach Sean Payton took back the offensive play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb.


              Coleman's second TD run gave Denver a 24-17 lead with 20 seconds left in the third quarter and his last one followed a turnover on downs at midfield by the Raiders.


              Mendoza's 7-yard strike to Jack Bech with 4:29 remaining got the Raiders within 31-24.


              Mendoza finished 18 of 37 for 267 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He was sacked five times.


              Bo Nix completed 19 of 35 passes for 225 yards with one TD and an interception. He connected with tight end Evan Engram six times for 74 yards.


              Las Vegas erased the final remnants of a 17-0 deficit when Mendoza hit tight end Ian Thomas for a 19-yard touchdown in the third quarter. The score came after Nix was stuffed by Maxx Crosby and Folorunso Fatukasi on a fourth-and-1 sneak from the Denver 39.


              The Raiders turned it over on downs at the Denver 46 early in the fourth quarter when Mendoza overthrew Jalen Nailor.


              Coming off their bye week, the healthy Broncos had their most productive first half of the season, jumping out to a 17-0 lead on Wil Lutz's 38-yard field goal, Adam Trautman's 1-yard touchdown grab and Coleman's 1-yard TD run.


              Denver's special teams blocked two of AJ Cole's punts, helping the Broncos win the field-position game in the first half. But Denver's defense, which drew coordinator Vance Joseph's ire during the week for having given up big plays against Carolina the last time out, surrendered two big plays that kept the Broncos from running away with it.

articles.headline: Bulls G Norman Powell sidelined by mild hamstring injury
articles.description: Bulls guard Norman Powell was ruled out against the Nuggets and will be reevaluated later in the week because of a mild right hamstring strain.
articles.headlineJa: ブルズのGノーマン・パウエル、軽度のハムストリング損傷により欠場
articles.descriptionJa: ブルズのガード、ノーマン・パウエルは、右ハムストリングの軽度の筋断裂によりナゲッツ戦を欠場。今週後半に状態を再評価する予定。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Bulls guard Norman Powell has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Nuggets because of a mild right hamstring strain.

Powell was injured during Friday night's 98-94 loss to the Washington Wizards. The Bulls said Powell will be evaluated later this week.

The 33-year-old Powell is averaging a team-high 20.8 points per game in his first season with Chicago. He scored 16 points against the Wizards on 7-for-18 shooting.

Powell signed a two-year deal with the Bulls in free agency that could be worth up to $45 million. The veteran guard played for the Miami Heat last season, averaging 21.7 points in 58 games while earning an All-Star selection for the first time.

Chicago rookie Caleb Wilson also missed the matchup with Denver. Wilson is working his way back from a broken right hand.

articles.headline: Alexander-Walker has 27 points as Hawks roll to 107-97 win over Pistons in off game for Cunningham
articles.description: — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points.
articles.headlineJa: アレクサンダー＝ウォーカーが27得点を挙げ、ホークスがピストンズに107-97で快勝（カニンガムは不振）
articles.descriptionJa: ニキール・アレクサンダー＝ウォーカーが27得点を記録。アトランタは第4クォーターを18-0のランで開始し、カデ・カニンガムがシーズンワーストの5得点に抑えられる中、ホークスは日曜日のデトロイト・ピストンズ戦を107-97で制した。
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points.


              Cunningham set a season high with 15 assists but a combination of early foul trouble and a sore knee combined to hold him to 20 points below his average of 25.6 as he made 2 of 9 shots. It was his first game of the season not scoring in double figures.


              Corey Kispert scored a season-high 18 points and Lu Dort had 16 in the Hawks' fourth straight win.


              Isaiah Joe led Detroit with 19 points. Ausar Thompson and John Collins had 18 and Paul Reed added 16.


              The Pistons led 85-74 at the start of the fourth quarter before the Hawks took a 92-85 with the 18 unanswered points. Joe's 3-pointer with 4:52 remaining ended Detroit's scoreless streak.


              Cunningham picked up two fouls in the first period and was called for his third foul early in the second. He was limited to 14 minutes in the first half while missing all three of his shots from the field.


              Cunningham scored his first points with a jumper off the glass early in the second half but continued to focus on setting up shots for teammates while receiving extra defensive attention from Dyson Daniels and the Hawks.


              Cunningham was included on Detroit's injury report with right knee soreness. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff said before the game protecting Cunningham was “the most important thing. He’s a competitor and wants to play. But it’s also our responsibility to just make sure that we’re protecting him at all costs.”


              Cunningham was held out of Detroit's 122-109 win at New Orleans on Wednesday night but scored 23 points in a 105-102 loss to Toronto on Friday night.


              Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings had 10 points after missing three games with a sore back.


              Up next
              Pistons: Play at Orlando on Tuesday night.


              Hawks: Visit Boston on Friday night.

articles.headline: USMNT's Cardoso scores as Atlético ease to win over Getafe
articles.description: Atlético Madrid bolstered their spot in third in LaLiga with a comfortable 3-0 win at Getafe on Sunday.
articles.body:
Atlético Madrid bolstered their spot in third in LaLiga with a comfortable 3-0 win at Getafe on Sunday.

A superb long-range strike by Álex Baena put Diego Simeone's team in front and Johnny Cardoso's 30th-minute tap-in increased Atlético's stranglehold on the contest in Madrid.

Getafe pushed for a way back into the contest, but Atlético stood firm and grabbed a third late on from the penalty spot via Alejandro Grimaldo to make it eight wins in nine league matches.

It took Atlético only 10 minutes to break the deadlock when Julián Álvarez controlled inside the area and teed up Baena, who let fly from 30 yards and found the bottom corner.

Atlético went close again immediately after from a corner, but Getafe's fortunate ended there with Cardoso able to double the visitors' lead in the 30th minute.

Álvarez sent in a dangerous delivery which Getafe goalkeeper David Soria failed to gather and Cardoso tapped in on the line.

Getafe pushed to reduce the deficit, but it remained 2-0 at halftime.

Simeone replaced Cardoso with Lee Kang-In for the second half and Baena almost made it 3-0 with one shot saved before he sent another off target.

Baena and Álvarez were taken off midway through the second half, but there was still time for Atlético to grab a third.

After substitute Alexander Sørloth headed wide, the Norwegian was brought down inside the area by Djene Dakonam and after a VAR review, Dakonam was sent off and Alejandro Grimaldo converted from 12 yards to move Atlético to 31 points on the season, two behind Real Madrid and five behind leaders Barcelona.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Bruno Fernandes disputes Leny Yoro red card in Liverpool's rout of Man United
articles.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was not happy with the officiating in Sunday's 4-0 drubbing at Liverpool.
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was not happy with the officiating in Sunday's 4-0 drubbing at Liverpool, insisting Leny Yoro's early challenge on Alexander Isak was "never a red card."

Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute by referee Sam Barrott for what was deemed a last-man foul that denied Isak a goalscoring opportunity following Matthijs de Ligt's mistake, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

The Reds went on to complete a comprehensive rout over the 10 men with further goals from Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Víctor Muñoz as Mauricio Pochettino's Red Devils reign got off to a miserable start at Anfield.

The new head coach said he took full ownership of the result but felt the Yoro sending off changed the course of the game, with his skipper in agreement and feeling the wrong decision had been reached.

The Portugal midfielder told BBC Sport: "I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card.

"I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.

"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."

articles.headline: Sources: Free agent Gabe Vincent, Kings finalizing deal
articles.description: Gabe Vincent is finalizing a deal with the Kings to fill their 15th roster spot, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
Free agent guard Gabe Vincent is finalizing a deal with the Sacramento Kings to fill their 15th roster spot, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Sunday.

The Kings have been in the market for backcourt depth after veteran Ben Simmons tore his Achilles in the preseason, leaving them without requisite help behind lottery pick Darius Acuff Jr., who is averaging an NBA-high 36.9 minutes per game.

Vincent, 30, is expected to join the Kings this week to begin his eighth NBA season. He played a combined 53 games for the Los Angeles Lakers and Atlanta Hawks last season, averaging 4.4 points and making 34.3% of his 3-point attempts in 16.6 minutes per game.

After two extended losing streaks in the opening month, the Kings sit at the bottom of the Western Conference standings with a 2-14 record, though they did upset the Boston Celtics 97-96 on Saturday to become the final NBA team to get a home win. In it, Acuff scored 23 points in 40 minutes. The Kings outscored the Celtics by 16 points when he was on the floor and were outscored by 15 in the eight minutes he was off it. 

Vincent has been signed, in part, to help in those non-Acuff minutes and provide some needed perimeter spacing. The Kings rank in the bottom 10 in the league in 3-point attempts and percentage. Vincent has made 459 career 3s.

articles.headline: Villarreal deny Nicolas Pépé eye surgery was due to viewing solar eclipse
articles.description: Villarreal have denied that Nicolas Pépé underwent eye surgery as a result of viewing the solar eclipse.
articles.body:
Villarreal have denied that Nicolas Pépé underwent eye surgery as a result of viewing the solar eclipse.

The Ivorian winger missed five games in October after undergoing the surgery, but the LaLiga club have refuted reports that this was due to viewing the phenomenon without the proper protection.

Such reports surfaced after footage on social media -- allegedly posted by Pépé himself -- appeared to show the former Arsenal man looking directly at the eclipse on Aug. 12, 2026, without a solar viewer.

"In light of recent reports published by various media outlets, Villarreal CF wishes to clarify that claims linking Nicolas Pepe's eye surgery to viewing the solar eclipse are completely false," the club said in a statement on Sunday.

"The procedure had been scheduled beforehand for reasons entirely unrelated to this event.

"The club calls for accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters concerning the health of its players."

Villarreal lost to both Liverpool and Real Madrid during the period in which Pépé was absent.

The 31-year-old has scored three goals in 12 games this season after one of the best campaigns of his career in 2025-26, in which he notched eight goals and 11 assists in 46 matches.

He joined Villarreal in 2024 from Trabzonspor after previously playing for the likes of Arsenal, Lille and Nice.

Iñigo Pérez's side are 10th in LaLiga having won four, drawn three and lost six matches.

articles.headline: Poch blames 'circumstances' in painful Man United loss to Liverpool
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino called for understanding of the "circumstances" that led to Manchester United suffering a 4-0 defeat Sunday against Liverpool in his first game as head coach.
articles.body:
LIVERPOOL, England -- Mauricio Pochettino called for understanding of the "circumstances" that led to Manchester United suffering a 4-0 defeat Sunday against Liverpool in his first game as head coach -- a loss which was the worst start for a United boss in 100 years.

United remain in the Premier League relegation zone after a humiliating result at Anfield which was sparked by Leny Yoro's eighth minute red card for a foul on Alexander Isak that referee Sam Barrott deemed to have denied a clear goalscoring opportunity.

With Yoro sent off, United were forced to face Andoni Iraola's team with 10 players for over 80 minutes and Pochettino, who stepped down from his role as coach of the United States to move to Old Trafford, said that the end result was a consequence of Yoro's dismissal.

"Today we concede four goals with 10 men and after playing 80 minutes at Anfield with 10 men," Pochettino told reporters. "I take responsibility for that, no worries, but I don't want to compare with the past. Now it is to talk about today

"But you have to look at circumstances. Otherwise to talk is so cheap. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action and 80 minutes to play more, do you think that is easy?

"Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances concede four goals or even more.

"We lost one game. We are not going to lose more than one the way we lost today. We feel the pain, but we keep working."

Pochettino said United should have had a penalty prior to Yoro's red card following a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo.

"I wasn't agreeing with the red card because I think the situation was when Isak control the ball, the ball wasn't in his control," Pochettino said. "The centre-back [Yoro] was running with him, Isak saw the control wasn't good and it is normal you delay, you stop to run, in that moment Yoro came from the back and it is like a touch like this and you go down.

"Never is a foul, but if you go two minutes before and the situation with Jacquet and Mbeumo and tell me?

"It was a penalty to Mbeumo, we can make mistake, no but we were punished and they were not."

Pochettino, meanwhile, defended his decision to start Matthijs de Ligt, despite the Netherlands defender having not started a Premier League for over a year due to a back injury. De Ligt was at fault for three goals in an error-strewn performance that questioned his selection.

"He was training," Pochettino said. "He played in the Champions League before the international duty and when we arrived, we saw the combinations.

"But I repeat again, with Jacquet it was penalty and that action after never come. One centre-back made a mistake, it was a mistake, wasn't punished and after we [De Ligt] made a mistake and was punished."

United are 19th in the Premier League and have now made their worst start to a season since 1972-73. But Pochettino insisted United have "lots of games to play" as they attempt to escape their perilous position.

articles.headline: Milan into top four as classy Pulisic solo goal caps Serie A rout
articles.description: AC Milan racked up their biggest win of the season under Ruben Amorim as Frosinone were beaten 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: プリシッチの鮮やかなソロゴールで大勝、ミランがトップ4入り
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日にサン・シーロで行われたフロジノーネ戦で、ACミランは5-1で勝利し、ルベン・アモリム監督のもとで今シーズン最大の勝利を挙げた。
articles.body:
AC Milan racked up their biggest win of the season under Ruben Amorim as Frosinone were beaten 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

It is now five wins in six matches for Milan, who climbed into Serie A's top four and to within five points of leaders Lazio.

It was a rampaging victory earned with room to spare, and was much needed following wins for Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus.

An own goal from Gabriele Calvani and a fourth goal of the season from Gonçalo Ramos made it 2-0 early on before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit for the visitors.

The second half quickly turned into a procession with goals from Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cissè making it 4-1 before Christian Pulisic got a goal to add some gloss to the scoreline.

Newly promoted Frosinone have been one of the surprise packages of the season, but dropped to seventh behind Juve after Luciano Spalletti's side extended their own unbeaten run to four games with a home win.

Calvani's own goal got Milan on their way, then Adrien Rabiot set up Ramos for a much-needed goal following a relatively slow start to life in Serie A.

The visitors hauled themselves back into contention midway through the first half through Masini, but Milan pulled clear in the second half with an excellent counter-attacking play.

Substitutes Jashari and Cisse made good on Milan's dominance before Pulisic's solo run and chipped finish completed the rout to wrap up the biggest win of Amorim's time in charge.

Information from PA was used in this recap.
